script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for December 31. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Here we are—Day 365.  You've shown up, day after day, to learn something new.  That might seem simple, but it's not.

Improving 1% per day means being 37 times better after a year. That's not motivation hype—it's mathematics. Daily learning isn't about any single lesson. It's about the cumulative effect of showing up, again and again. Your brain physically changes when you learn consistently.  New neural pathways form and strengthen.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: What you did this year wasn't just consume information.  You built something—a practice, a habit, a way of being.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Year Complete - The Growth Inventory.

Here's your activity: Write a letter to yourself from one year ago. Tell past-you what you've learned, how you've grown, and what you're grateful for from this year of daily lessons. Keep it somewhere you'll find it next year. This helps you acknowledge and celebrate a full year of consistent learning.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about 365 days of growing can be applied to year complete - the growth inventory. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
